summary: Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who studied at Yale University (BA, ~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (PhD, ~1969–1976). In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who was a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education in 2005 and served as Executive Director of UBC's Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2005).

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. He served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Albright College (attested 2007).

Victor H. Mair worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD, ~1974–1976). He was an assistant professor at Harvard (~1976–1979) before becoming Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Victor Henry was an Indologist and linguist who taught at the University of Douai (~1884–1887), the University of Lille (~1887–1888), and the École Centrale de Lille. In 1888, he became professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris.

Victor Turner worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at University College London and the University of Manchester (PhD, ~1950–1955). His career included posts at Manchester (~1955–1963), Cornell (1963), Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Vidya Dehejia is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge (~1963–1968). Her posts include Columbia University (associate professor 1982; professor 2002) and chief curator at the Smithsonian Institution (1994).

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Allahabad under Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya and at Gorakhpur. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1971) and served as vice-chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Vijayalakshmi Mani is a scholar of Indology and history who studied as a PhD scholar under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2026).

Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist and Central Asian studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Copenhagen (1859–1869). He served there as Privatdozent (1869), associate professor (1875), and Professor (1887–1913), later becoming President of the Royal Danish Academy (1909).

Vinay Lal is a scholar of history and Indology who studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1980–1984). In ~1993, he became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist who studied at Charles University (~1903–1907) under Josef Zubatý and Moriz Winternitz. He held academic posts at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts from ~1918 to 1952.

Vincent Arthur Smith was an Indologist and historian who earned a doctorate from Trinity College Dublin (-1919). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) and later as a curator at the University of Oxford and St John's College (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA (1996) and PhD (2012) from Leiden University, also studying under Lucia Dolce. He served as a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lausanne (~1995–2003) under Tom Tillemans, worked at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and became Directeur d’études at EPHE in ~2015.

Vincent Goossaert is a historian of Chinese religion and Sinology who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997). He held research posts at the CNRS (~1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at EPHE in ~2012.

Vincent Lefèvre is an Indologist and historian who studied under Bruno Dagens and at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (HDR, 2007) and the École Nationale des Chartes. He has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE (PhD, -2012) and under Seishi Karashima and Cristina Scherrer-Schaub. He held posts at EFEO (attested 2021) and the University of Tokyo and Göttingen Academy (attested 2026).
Vincenzo Vergiani is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raffaele Torella. Around 2008, he took up a post as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge.
